title: KYE Evidence Pack
description: Self-contained, signed bundle that captures everything needed to replay and verify a single decision: a reference to the decision map, the immutable input blob, the signed state of the world used during evaluation, the supporting signals, signatures over the bundle, and a reference to the replay context seal. Auditors and regulators consume this as the unit of evidence.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Every runtime emitter stamps it and every canonical example carries it; pinned with const so the envelope cannot claim a schema it is not.

id.description: Stable URN of the evidence pack.

version.description: Schema major version. Pinned to 1 for kye.evidence.pack.v1.

decision_id.description: URN of the decision this pack provides evidence for.

decision_map_ref.description: Content-addressable reference to the kye.evidence.decision_map.v1 instance for this decision (e.g. its id or CID).

inputs_blob_ref.description: Content-addressable reference to the immutable, canonical-encoded inputs blob the engine consumed.

signed_state.description: Signed snapshot of the relevant state-of-the-world used during evaluation (grants in force, policies live, principal status, etc.).

state_hash.description: Hash over the canonical encoding of the state snapshot.

state_ref.description: Optional content-addressable reference to the full state snapshot blob.

signer.description: KYEID of the entity that signed the snapshot.

signals.description: External signals consumed during evaluation (risk scores, telemetry, attestations). Each carries provenance.

id.description: Locally-unique signal identifier inside the pack.

source.description: KYEID or URN of the signal producer.

payload_hash.description: Hash of the signal's canonical payload.

observed_at.description: Time the signal was observed by the engine.

signatures.description: Signatures binding the pack contents together (typically engine + principal countersignature).

replay_seal_ref.description: Content-addressable reference to the kye.replay.context_seal.v1 captured at decision time.

created_at.description: Time the evidence pack was assembled.

decided_in_region.description: §16 §12 Residency-proof (2026-06-10). The canonical residency region (kye:dictionary:data-residency region term) in which this decision was EVALUATED — the region-pinning PEP resolved the request and ran the policy here. Distinct from jurisdictions[] (legal jurisdiction): this is the infra deployment region. A regulator re-derives, from the pack alone, that the tenant's decision was made in-jurisdiction. Stamped by the region-pinning PEP (internal).

stored_in_region.description: §16 §12 Residency-proof (2026-06-10). The canonical residency region in which this evidence pack + decision record were PERSISTED (the region-pinned D1 + jurisdiction-restricted R2 bucket declared in internal). MUST equal decided_in_region unless the pack carries a cross_border record with a lawful_basis. A regulator re-derives that the evidence was stored in-jurisdiction.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions this evidence pack is scoped to — values from internal Used to filter regulator-facing replay: an ICO subpoena receives only UK-scoped packs; an OCR subpoena receives only US-scoped packs. The pack includes BOTH the data-subject jurisdiction and every processing-region the call touched, so cross-border calls surface their full route.

subject_jurisdiction_canonical.description: Jurisdiction of the data subject (where applicable) — drives lawful-basis selection + retention floor. Resolves against internal Optional in v1.x; required in v2.

cross_border.description: Cross-border transfer record. Populated automatically when subject_jurisdiction_canonical differs from any element of jurisdictions[] (i.e. the call crossed a boundary). Carries the lawful basis for the transfer so GDPR Art. 44-49 transfer-impact assessment is automatic.

lawful_basis.description: GDPR Art. 44-49 transfer mechanism. Mirrors EDPB Recommendations 01/2020.

basis_ref.description: URN or URL of the documentary evidence backing the lawful basis (e.g. SCC version, BCR approval reference).

memory_basis.description: §31 Memory Authority. Every agent-memory record the decision relied upon — as action evidence or as decision context — with the recall-time admissibility verdict. Empty/absent = the action relied on no memory. A regulator can re-derive whether the memory the agent acted on was authorised, current, scoped, consented and provenance-backed.

memory_id.description: URN of the kye.agent_memory.v1 record relied upon.

content_hash.description: Pins the exact memory version relied upon (matches kye.agent_memory.v1.content_hash).

used_as.description: Whether the memory was cited as evidence justifying the action, or only as background context informing it.

admissibility_state.description: Recall-time verdict (canonical enum — single declaration here). MEMORY_ADMISSIBLE/MEMORY_NOT_ADMISSIBLE are the terminal verdicts; the remainder are the reason states that drive them. A non-admissible memory used as action_evidence maps to the Action-Admissibility inadmissibility class `inadmissible_memory`.

reasons.description: Zero or more contributing reason states when admissibility_state is a terminal verdict (e.g. [MEMORY_STALE, MEMORY_SCOPE_EXCEEDED]).

coordinate.description: WHERE in the governed estate this decision happened, sealed at decision time — the §0.52 coordinate (plane × class × kye-id) plus the `t` axis that says which version of the entity map it was resolved against. Without it a pack answers what was decided and when, but a holder must consult a LIVE registry to answer where, which is the same non-portability `resolution` exists to fix: offline (§0.47) there is no registry to consult, and online the registry has moved on, so a coordinate resolved at read time silently describes today's estate rather than the one the decision was made in. Sealing the COMPUTED value here does not create a second source of truth for position (§0/§0.10) — the coordinate index is explicit that a coordinate is a JOIN never stored on a record, and this is the same freezing-a-derived-fact-at-t that decision_map_ref and signed_state already do. `t.basis` is the discriminator that makes it checkable rather than merely asserted: a verifier that recomputes the same basis can resolve plane/class/kye_id against that exact map, and one that recomputes a different basis reports that the map moved instead of guessing. A basis naming a map the verifier does not hold (a tenant's own estate rather than KYE's) is reported as unverifiable-here, never silently skipped. Additive and optional — a pack without it is still valid evidence, just not self-locating.

plane.description: §33 IP/OSS plane of the acting entity's artefact, as derived at decision time.

class.description: The entity's artefact_class (§0.36 namespace) at decision time.

kye_id.description: The entity whose position this is — the acting principal (§0.30: an agent is a principal exactly like a human or a system).

origin.description: How `class` and `kye_id` were determined. Present because two determinations answer different questions and a consumer that cannot tell them apart reads a structural class as a semantic one: a registry-sourced class says WHAT the entity is (worker, surface, endpoint), a path-derived class says only that the artefact exists and is a file or a folder. Stating it is the difference between an honest coordinate and a silently-downgraded one (§0.31).

t.description: The fourth axis. Two facts, deliberately not merged: `at` is the instant the position was true, `basis` is the map version it was true against. A timestamp alone cannot be re-resolved (there is no way to reconstruct what the registry said then); a basis alone cannot be ordered.

at.description: When the coordinate was resolved. Normally the DECISION instant, not the pack-assembly instant — the position that matters is where the entity sat when the decision was made, and the two differ whenever assembly is deferred.

basis.description: kye.coordinate_index.v1 `t.basis` of the entity map this coordinate was resolved against.

resolution.description: The RESOLVED content every *_ref field points at, carried inside the pack — the peer of kye.authority_proof_bundle.v1.resolution (constitution/53-COHESION-CASCADE.md §3.3). Without it this pack is a manifest of pointers: decision_map_ref, inputs_blob_ref and replay_seal_ref resolve only inside KYE storage, so a holder can hold the pack but cannot verify OFFLINE what it points at, and WORM-storing it (§30) freezes the pointer while its target stays mutable — the one thing a seal exists to prevent. Each member carries a per-member content address (sha256 over the member's canonical bytes), which is the evidence pack's offline tamper-evidence: recomputing it detects any post-resolution change and NAMES which ref changed, with no KYE service in the loop (§0.47). This is additive and optional — a pack without it is still valid, but is portable pointers, not portable evidence. Distinct from the pack's own seal: the pack `id` is content-addressed over the whole body (resolution included) and `signatures[]` bind it; `resolution` makes the refs' targets travel and be independently checkable.

resolved_at.description: When the refs were resolved into members. Normally equals the pack's created_at.

member_order.description: The ref-field names, in a declared order. Declared rather than implied because any consumer that concatenates or enumerates members is order-sensitive, and 'obvious' orderings are exactly what drifts between implementations.

ref_field.description: Which *_ref property of this pack this member resolves (e.g. decision_map_ref).

ref.description: The reference carried in that field — kept so the resolution is auditable against the pointer it replaces. The sha256 is KYE's content address of the resolved content and does not claim to reproduce a ref's own native address (e.g. an IPFS CID).

sha256.description: Content address of this member's canonical bytes. Per-member so a tampered member is identified individually, not merely detected somewhere in the pack.

content.description: The resolved object itself — the decision map, the inputs blob, the replay context seal. This is the evidence; the ref is metadata about it.

unresolved.description: Ref fields deliberately NOT resolved, each with a reason. Present so an incomplete pack is HONEST rather than silently thin (§70): a verifier reports partial resolution instead of passing a pack whose missing half nobody declared. An empty array is the resting state. A ref the schema makes REQUIRED may never be declared here.
